sections.overview: Pseudeuophrys erratica is a small jumping spider in the family Salticidae, recorded across Europe and much of Asia.
sections.identification: Adults are only a few millimetres long. Males have contrasting black-and-white palps; females can be difficult to distinguish from related Pseudeuophrys without close examination.
sections.habitat: It has been recorded on the ground and on tree trunks, including dead wood; British accounts also report it under bark and stones.
sections.diet: The references consulted do not provide a species-specific account of its prey.
sections.behavior: Field accounts report that males and juveniles are more readily encountered than females; this may affect the chance of identifying the species in surveys.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted do not provide species-specific reproductive details.
sections.ecology: It is widespread in Europe and Asia, with an introduced population reported in the United States; local French assessments list it as Least Concern.
sections.conservation: French Red List assessments classify it as Least Concern; this is a national assessment, not a global IUCN category.
